Thought: Let me analyze each of these compounds:

A. 2-pentanone: This is a ketone with 5 carbon atoms where the carbonyl group (C=O) is at the 2nd position.

B. methyl ethyl ketone: This is the common name for butanone, which has a methyl group (CH3) and an ethyl group (CH2CH3) attached to the carbonyl carbon. Its formula is C4H8O.

C. methyl propyl ketone: This is a ketone with a methyl group (CH3) and a propyl group (CH3CH2CH2) attached to the carbonyl carbon. Its formula is C5H10O.

D. pentan-2-one: This is another name for 2-pentanone, where the carbonyl group is at the 2nd position of a 5-carbon chain.

Now, let me check if these compounds are the same or different:
- A (2-pentanone) and D (pentan-2-one) are the same compound, just different naming conventions.
- C (methyl propyl ketone) is also the same as 2-pentanone/pentan-2-one, as it has a methyl group on one side of the carbonyl and a propyl group on the other.
- B (methyl ethyl ketone) is different - it has 4 carbon atoms total (butanone), while the others all have 5 carbon atoms.

Therefore, methyl ethyl ketone (B) is distinct from the others.
